exposure: maternal plasma biomarkers of APAP exposure
outcome: child attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnosis
cohort: The study included 307 African American mother-child pairs.
finding: Detection of APAP in second trimester maternal plasma was associated with higher odds for child ADHD diagnosis, and prenatal APAP exposure was linked to specific placental gene expression changes, including immune system upregulation in females and oxidative phosphorylation downregulation in both sexes.
